final_proof:
Let \(h=\frac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr)\). All the operations in this definition are pointwise. Thus, for every \(s\in S\),
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(f(s)+g(s)+|f(s)-g(s)|\bigr).
\]
Fix an arbitrary \(s\in S\). Since the real numbers are totally ordered, either \(f(s)\ge g(s)\) or \(f(s)<g(s)\).

If \(f(s)\ge g(s)\), then \(f(s)-g(s)\ge0\), so \(|f(s)-g(s)|=f(s)-g(s)\). Consequently,
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(f(s)+g(s)+f(s)-g(s)\bigr)=f(s)=\max\{f(s),g(s)\}=(f\vee g)(s).
\]
If \(f(s)<g(s)\), then \(f(s)-g(s)<0\), so \(|f(s)-g(s)|=-(f(s)-g(s))=g(s)-f(s)\). Consequently,
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(f(s)+g(s)+g(s)-f(s)\bigr)=g(s)=\max\{f(s),g(s)\}=(f\vee g)(s).
\]
Hence \(h(s)=(f\vee g)(s)\) for every \(s\in S\). By extensionality of functions (both functions have domain \(S\) and codomain \(\mathbb R\)),
\[
f\vee g=h=\frac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr),
\]
as required.
